elements.element: Customer owns deliverables/work product created for it
elements.evidence: "shall be owned by Corio, including all intellectual property rights in the Developments" (carve-out returning ownership to Commerce One deleted)

elements.element: Vendor assigns any claimed ownership in deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "Commerce One hereby assigns all rights in and to such Developments to Corio"
"Subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence grant of any kind appears in the redlined clause; the comment itself notes "there is no licence back"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: Clause addresses only "DEVELOPMENTS" and pre-existing materials; no Customer Data rights language anywhere in the clause
"enhancements, modifications or derivative works to the Software itself which may be developed jointly by the parties ... shall be negotiated by the parties" — joint development ownership left open

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: Only "pre-existing ownership of any materials or technology provided to Corio" is preserved; no generic tools/know-how carve-out

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to deliverables
elements.evidence: No licence grant present in the clause

elements.element: Licence rights to use, modify and sublicense for Customer's business

reasons: The locked preferred level is incomplete: the redline secures Customer ownership and the assignment, but adds no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in the Developments, no Customer Data rights statement, and no express no-joint-ownership term (the final sentence still leaves jointly developed Software derivatives to future negotiation).

Deterministic check confirms the preferred embedded-IP licence element fails: a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables is required, not merely reliance on the opening pre-existing-ownership proviso and Section 2.8.
Fallback is also not satisfied (no generic tools/know-how allocation and no use/modify/sublicense licence), so the clause does not sit at either bargain.

Minimality gate failed: the single replacement rewrote 0.788 of the anchored span (limit 0.600); a tighter anchor deleting only "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights," would suffice, and re-inserting "all" was unnecessary.

Intent is preserved: pre-existing IP, the Employee NDA/Invention covenants, the non-disclosure covenant and the future-negotiation sentence all remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
